verdict.rationale: Pulumi's testing guide documents three first-party testing modes. Unit tests run in memory and mock all external calls, so nothing touches real infrastructure. Property tests run resource-level assertions during deployment, and integration tests deploy ephemeral infrastructure, all written with native frameworks such as Mocha or NUnit. Separately, `pulumi preview` offers a dry-run that changes nothing, but that is a preview, not sandboxed test isolation. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of the testing workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write automated tests for my infrastructure code and run them without touching production

citations.quote: Unit Tests are fast in-memory tests that mock all external calls. Property Tests run resource-level assertions while infrastructure is being deployed. Integration Tests deploy ephemeral infrastructure and run external tests against it.
Unit tests are authored in the same language as the Pulumi program under test. You can use your favorite test and mock frameworks like Mocha for Node.js or NUnit for .NET.
Because Pulumi uses general purpose programming languages to provision cloud resources, you can take advantage of native testing frameworks
